title: Battery-Aware Regret Greedy with Large-Neighborhood Repair
hypothesis: Replacing the baseline earliest-fit greedy (which ignores task weight, battery, turnaround time and energy) with a constructive regret-based insertion that scores each feasible insertion by its exact marginal contribution to the mission objective (dominated by weighted completion, plus count, release-to-completion latency and energy cost, normalised by the slew+duration time it consumes and penalised by regret versus the task's next-best satellite opportunity), followed by time-budgeted large-neighbourhood search (random/worst-contribution/time-window destroy and regret reinsertion, plus 1-for-1 and 1-for-2 task swaps on each satellite chain), will raise combined_score by at least 5 points over program_0 on the 7 development missions while returning a sim.check-valid plan on every mission, because it targets high-weight tasks before their scarce feasible opportunities are consumed by low-weight early tasks and repairs the myopic choices a single greedy pass makes.

title: Chain-DP Ejection Repair on Battery-Safe Insertion Core
hypothesis: Retaining the feasibility-by-construction battery-safe weighted insertion core that achieved 7/7 valid plans, replacing part of generic destroy-and-repair with exact per-satellite chain re-optimisation will raise score: for each satellite, a weighted interval-scheduling DP over its candidate opportunities (slew-feasible transitions, exact marginal score gain including WCR/CR/TAT/energy terms, battery-feasibility checked on the DP result) can optimally drop low-value blockers and insert 1-for-2/1-for-3 ejections that regret-greedy plus random LNS misses, lifting mean WCR from 0.6905 toward >=0.71 and combined_score by at least +1.0 over the 72.79 prior best without any validity or runtime regression.

title: Density-Scored Widened Chain-DP with Cross-Satellite Ejection
hypothesis: The cycle-2 chain-DP improved WCR from 0.6905 to 0.7086 and combined_score from 72.79 to 73.67 but narrowly missed its targets because its per-satellite DP candidate pool was too narrow and its node values did not price occupied slew-plus-duration time, so high-weight unscheduled tasks blocked by one or two low-density incumbents on another satellite were never considered. Retaining the battery-safe insertion core and widening the DP pool to selected plus overlapping unscheduled plus top per-task alternatives, scoring DP nodes by exact-objective-aligned gain per occupied time, adding depth-2 cross-satellite ejection/reinsertion, and shifting most of the time budget to repeated DP rounds allocated by unscheduled weight density will raise mean WCR to at least 0.73 and combined_score to at least 74.8 while preserving 7/7 validity.

title: Multi-Satellite Segment DP with Heavy-Task Ejection Chains
hypothesis: Cycle-3 widened per-satellite chain-DP reached 74.3238 (WCR 0.7207) with diminishing gains (+0.88, then +0.65) because each satellite's chain is re-optimised in isolation: a heavy unscheduled task blocked on one satellite often stays blocked even though a coordinated swap across neighbouring satellites in the same time segment could place it. Jointly re-optimising contiguous high-density time segments across 2-3 satellites at once, seeded with depth-2/3 ejection chains that displace low weight-per-occupied-time incumbents for the heaviest unscheduled tasks and try to reinsert the displaced tasks on partner satellites, and accepting moves only on an exact positive objective delta (weight, completion, turnaround and energy terms), will raise mean WCR to at least 0.735 and combined_score to at least 75.4 on the 7 development missions while preserving 7/7 validity, whereas simply enlarging the per-satellite DP pool or running more generic LNS rounds will not.

title: Boundary-Aware Segment DP with Perturbed Iterated Ejection
hypothesis: Cycle-4 segment DP gained only +0.16 (74.32 to 74.48, mean WCR 0.7207 to 0.7239) because it ignored boundary neighbours outside each segment and its try_insert step dropped DP-chosen observations. If segment DP is made boundary-aware (fixed predecessor/successor anchors with exact slew-gap and battery state carried into and out of the segment), DP choices are applied verbatim instead of re-filtered, the pool adds per-task alternatives ranked by exact objective gain per occupied slew-plus-duration time, and the remaining budget runs perturbed iterated ejection (restart-from-best, seeded perturbation of low-density scheduled tasks, 1-for-3 ejection for the heaviest unscheduled decile, strict cumulative TAT cap) with iterations allocated in proportion to unscheduled weight density so weak segments/missions get more work, then mean WCR will rise from 0.7239 to at least 0.74 and combined_score from 74.4827 to at least 75.5 on the 7 development missions, with 7/7 validity, no TAT/PC regression, and the same mission-agnostic rules generalising to sealed missions.

title: Scarcity-Aware Heavy-Task Reservation with Task-Preserving Relocation
hypothesis: The cycle-4/5 plateau (74.4827 then 74.4373, mean WCR ~0.723, weakest mission unchanged at 69.7516) is not caused by segment-DP boundaries or too few ejection rounds, but by heavy tasks with scarce access (few feasible opportunities, few eligible satellites, or narrow time spread) losing DP value trade-offs to denser light tasks and by scheduled tasks occupying their worst opportunity. Seeding from the cycle-4 best, reserving scarce heavy tasks before density DP, and relocating scheduled tasks to alternative opportunities of the same task to free gaps/reduce turnaround without losing completion, accepted only on exact positive whole-plan objective delta, will raise combined_score by at least 1.0 and mean WCR to at least 0.74 while preserving validity, turnaround and energy discipline.

title: Lagrangian-Priced Global Construction with Priced Segment DP
hypothesis: Cycles 4-6 plateaued at 74.44-74.48 because scarce heavy tasks are already lost during myopic construction and cannot be recovered by post-hoc segment DP, ejection, reservation or relocation (cycle-6 final: 74.4810, mean WCR 0.7238, weakest mission unchanged at 69.7552). If opportunity selection is instead guided during construction by iteratively updated Lagrangian prices - a per-task price for duplicate-task contention, a per-satellite time-bin price for slot congestion, and a battery-scarcity price - then priced segment DP will reserve contended satellite time for high-value tasks whose true opportunity cost is currently invisible to gain-per-time greedy scoring, raising mean WCR to at least 0.74 and combined_score to at least 75.5 without validity, TAT or PC regression on sealed missions of the same kind.

title: Latency-Aware Lagrangian Priced Construction with Cumulative TAT Budget
hypothesis: Cycle-7 Lagrangian priced construction broke the 74.44-74.48 plateau (75.1203, mean WCR 0.7359 vs 0.7239, weakest 70.1094 vs 69.7516) but raised mean TAT to 1077.60s from 955.81s because its duplicate/time-bin/battery prices underweight marginal turnaround. Adding an explicit latency dual to the priced utility - the exact marginal TAT (and PC) cost of each insertion and segment-DP node, with its multiplier escalated by subgradient steps whenever the best feasible primal exceeds the mission's unpriced-incumbent TAT, run as a small deterministic multiplier portfolio - plus a cumulative whole-plan TAT budget on every acceptance, will retain most of the priced WCR gain while recovering at least 75s of mean TAT, lifting combined_score by at least 1.0 over 75.1203 on new missions of the same kind.

title: WCR-First Priced Portfolio with Per-Mission Latency Selection and Loose TAT Ceiling
hypothesis: A single latency price trades WCR for TAT uniformly across missions (cycle 7: WCR 0.7359/TAT 1077.60 at 75.1203; cycle 8 strong latency: WCR 0.7281/TAT 972.58 at 74.7406), but the profitable latency strength varies per mission. If the existing priced-construction rounds are instead run as a deterministic portfolio spanning zero-to-full latency price, each round's feasible primal plan is retained and selected per mission by exact whole-plan score, and only the winner is polished under a loose winner-relative TAT ceiling with a CR guard, then the solver recovers cycle-7 WCR while retaining much of cycle-8's TAT recovery, beating 75.1203 on combined score and lifting the weakest mission.

title: Perturbed Priced Portfolio with Dual Averaging and Unguarded Exact Polish
hypothesis: Cycle 7 priced construction (75.1203, WCR 0.7359, TAT 1077.60) is the best seed, but cycles 8-9 show latency-priced variants trade away more WCR than their TAT gain repays (74.7406 and 74.9711) and TAT ceilings/CR guards block otherwise exact-positive polish updates. Keeping the latency price at exactly the cycle-7 setting and instead improving the contention duals themselves - dual-averaged subgradient updates over more rounds plus deterministic perturbations of the duplicate/time-bin/battery prices that generate diverse feasible primals, per-mission selection by the exact whole-plan score, and all remaining time given to winner-only polish accepting only exact positive whole-plan deltas with no TAT ceiling or CR guard - will find better WCR-first primal basins and retain polish gains, raising combined score without repeating the latency tradeoff.

title: Battery-Aware Weighted Greedy with Repair and Local Search
hypothesis: Replacing the baseline time-order greedy (which ignores task weight, energy, and opportunity cost) with a battery-feasible insertion greedy scored by marginal mission-score gain per unit slew-plus-energy cost, followed by deterministic destroy-and-repair / swap local search under the 60s budget, will raise combined_score by selecting more high-weight and early tasks without battery or slew violations, and will generalize to sealed missions because all parameters are computed from the given world rather than per-mission constants.

title: Adaptive Regret LNS Using Full Time Budget Seeded From Best Greedy Plan
hypothesis: Program_1 is valid on 7/7 missions at 75.33 but stops after at most 40 destroy-and-repair rounds (max_solve_s 10.37s of the 60s limit), leaving WCR 0.732 and CR 0.792 with the weakest mission at 70.42. Replacing that fixed-round loop with a deadline-driven adaptive large-neighbourhood search seeded from program_1's construction - multiple deterministic destroy operators (worst-efficiency, satellite-segment, time-cluster, related-task), regret-2 repair scored by exact marginal WCR/CR/TAT/PC delta, 1-for-1 and 1-for-2 swap/ejection moves, adaptive operator weights, and restart-from-best on stagnation, run until a deadline derived from time_limit_s while retaining cached-gap and conservative-battery feasibility-by-construction - will raise combined_score by at least 1.0 point over 75.33, driven by higher WCR/CR, with no invalid mission on development or sealed missions of the same kind.

title: Weight-First Ejection Chains With TAT-Disciplined Acceptance
hypothesis: Seeding from the best ALNS program (combined 76.0726, mean WCR 0.7404, mean TAT regressed 961->1041) and shifting most of the search budget from generic destroy-and-repair to aggressive weight-first ejection chains will raise weighted completion without further turnaround regression: repeatedly taking the heaviest unscheduled tasks and inserting each by ejecting 1 or 2 low weight-per-occupied-time incumbents on a feasible satellite chain, accepted only on exact full-plan delta that is positive and does not worsen mean turnaround beyond a small tolerance, should achieve combined_score >= 77.0 with mean WCR >= 0.755 while keeping all 7 missions valid.

title: Perturbed Iterated Ejection With Cumulative Turnaround Budget
hypothesis: Seeding from the best weight-first ejection program (combined 76.4582, mean WCR 0.7499, mean TAT 1028.6, max_solve_s 20.17), replacing its single ejection pass with deadline-driven iterated ejection — deterministic perturbation kicks from the best-ever plan, 1-for-3 ejection reserved for the heaviest unscheduled decile, and a hard cumulative turnaround budget that rejects any accepted state whose mean TAT contribution would push the plan above the cycle-3 level minus a margin — will spend the unused ~30s productively, raise mean WCR to at least 0.760 and combined score to at least 77.2, and bring mean TAT to at most 1000 without losing validity on any mission, because the prior pass raised WCR on all 7 missions but exhausted improving moves quickly and only reduced TAT from 1040.6 to 1028.6.

title: TAT-Directed Retiming With CR-Guarded Heavy Ejection
hypothesis: Seeded from the cycle-4 best (combined 76.5967, mean WCR 0.7532, mean CR 0.7947, mean TAT 1026.81, 7/7 valid), the binding losses are now turnaround itself and the CR cost of heavy-task displacement, not search time: generic perturbation kicks added only +0.14 despite using the full deadline. Actively retiming already-scheduled observations to earlier feasible opportunities for the same task (and swapping a scheduled observation to a different feasible opportunity of the same task on the same satellite) will directly reduce mean TAT and open earlier gaps, while CR-guarded heavy ejection (accept a heavy insertion only if the exact whole-plan delta is positive AND mission CR does not drop below the seed-plan CR minus 0.002 and ejected incumbents are first offered regret reinsertion) will convert the freed gaps into heavy completions without repeating the cycle-4 CR regression (0.7951 to 0.7947). Together these should reach combined >=77.0 with mean TAT <=1005 and mean WCR >=0.758 while preserving 7/7 validity.

title: Deadline-Exhaustive Weakest-First Repaid Retiming and Ejection
hypothesis: Cycle-5 retiming under strict positive exact-delta acceptance rarely fired (earlier opportunities raise slew/power cost) and early no-progress termination stopped at 37.78s versus 49.74s for cycle-4, losing weighted completion (76.5566/0.7515 vs 76.5967/0.7532). If the cycle-4 battery-safe iterated-ejection core is kept, retiming is allowed as a bounded temporary power-cost increase only when the freed turnaround is repaid within the same local move by an exact-score-positive reinsertion, a completion-rate floor and cumulative turnaround cap guard every acceptance, and search continues to the deadline reserve with effort allocated inside each world to the satellites/time-segments carrying the most unscheduled weight, then mean weighted completion and turnaround will improve simultaneously over the 76.5967 best without regressing completion or validity on unseen missions.

title: Scarcity-Ordered Cross-Satellite Migration Rescue For Heavy Tasks
hypothesis: Cycles 4-6 plateaued at combined 76.43-76.60 (best 76.5967, mean WCR 0.7532, mean TAT 1026.81) because same-satellite ejection, perturbation kicks and retiming treat blockers locally: a heavy unscheduled task whose few feasible opportunities are blocked stays unscheduled even when its blockers could move to another satellite or slot. Ordering unscheduled tasks by opportunity scarcity (fewest feasible opportunities and highest blocker contention, tie-broken by weight) and rescuing them first via cross-satellite migration chains - relocating 1-2 low weight-per-occupied-time blockers to feasible slots on other satellites (or other opportunities of the same task) before inserting the heavy task, accepted only as one atomic bundle with positive exact whole-plan delta, CR floor and cumulative TAT cap - will unlock heavy tasks that local ejection cannot, raising mean WCR to at least 0.760 and combined score to at least 76.90 without TAT/CR regression. Removing the repaid-retiming pass (diagnosed overhead in cycle 6) frees the majority of the deadline for migration rescue.

title: Contention-Priced Construction With Protected Iterated Ejection
hypothesis: Heavy scarce tasks are lost during initial construction, not recoverable by post-hoc moves: post-hoc scarcity reservation/relocation scored 74.4810 with the weakest mission unchanged, repaid retiming scored 76.4283, and cross-satellite migration rescue scored 76.2903 (TAT improved to 994.20 but WCR/CR fell) versus the cycle-4 best of 76.5967 (WCR 0.7532, CR 0.7947, TAT 1026.81), all below their targets. Pricing satellite-time contention during construction — scarce/heavy tasks claim slots before congested low-value tasks consume them, with dual-style congestion penalties updated over 2-3 priced construction restarts — will raise WCR without the score cost of truncating ejection, provided iterated ejection retains at least 70% of the post-construction budget and every priced plan competes against the unmodified cycle-4 plan under exact whole-plan scoring.

title: TAT-Budgeted Weight-Aware Pricing With Pareto-Guarded Selection
hypothesis: Cycle-8 contention-priced construction gained only +0.032 over its seed (76.6287 vs 76.5967, mean WCR 0.7534, mean TAT 1033.65) because its prices underweight latency and priced plans were selected by exact score alone, so congestion gains were repaid in turnaround. If the priced insertion score is weight-aware (task weight discounted by the weighted contention it blocks, boosted by opportunity scarcity), charges lambda_TAT times the incremental turnaround with lambda_TAT raised whenever a construction's cumulative TAT exceeds a budget set from the seed plan, and plans are selected from a Pareto pool that requires TAT non-regression as well as exact-score improvement, then priced construction should add weighted completion without the TAT regression, and protected iterated ejection on the selected plan should push combined_score to at least 76.90 with mean WCR >= 0.758 and mean TAT <= 1010 on the 7 development missions and generalise to sealed missions.

title: Seed-Anchored Election With Full-Budget Perturbed Ejection
hypothesis: Contention-priced construction in cycle 8 added only +0.032 over its cycle-4 seed (76.6287 vs 76.5967, WCR 0.7534 vs 0.7532) and cycle 9's TAT-budgeted weight-aware pricing with Pareto guard regressed to 75.7116 (WCR 0.7351), so priced starts rarely earn their construction/selection cost. If, per world, the cycle-8 seed construction and one priced construction are both built and compared by exact whole-plan score, the priced plan is discarded unless it beats the seed by at least 0.05 exact points, all remaining budget (at least 85% when priced loses, at least 70% when it wins) is returned to perturbed iterated ejection from the elected incumbent, and the ejection cumulative-TAT cap is loosened to +2% over the elected incumbent under a CR floor of incumbent CR minus 0.002 with strictly positive exact-delta acceptance, then mean WCR and combined score will exceed cycle 8 (76.6287 / WCR 0.7534 / CR 0.7955 / TAT 1033.65) without validity or runtime loss on unseen missions.
